title: Finite local models and bounded constructibility under normalized encoding
statement: For a finite discrete commutative ring A, a scheme T, and any Encoding e of [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding], an internal module has a finite constant local model exactly when its fixed scalar image has ordinaryLocalModel. For every internal derived object K, constantModelBoundedConstructible holds exactly when ordinaryBoundedConstructible holds for its image under the actual termwise fixed scalar derived equivalence. Covers, finite constructible stratifications, the affine-local convention on non-qcqs schemes, and boundedness agree exactly.

source.place: Coefficient-identification argument, steps 8--9, without the separately treated Tor condition.

proof.text: The coefficient family in step 1 is compatible with pullback: the universe-general canonicalAbelianMap_naturality of [lem-sf-finite-discrete-encoding-naturality] says that its section maps commute with the direct-image coefficient map for every scheme morphism and every test object. For $h:U\to T$, write $b_h:h^{-1}A_T\xrightarrow{\sim}A_U$ for the canonical constant-sheaf map. The cited section equation says $\eta_h c_T=(h_*c_U)\eta_h^{\mathrm{const}}$. Taking adjoint transposes gives $c_U b_h=\alpha_h(h^{-1}c_T)$, an equality of maps $h^{-1}A_T\to p_U^*\underline A$. In the formulas of [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], both pullbacks are the inverse-image abelian sheaf with scalars extended along this same ring map. Using the balanced tensor comparison of step 5 gives $E_Uh^*\cong h^*E_T$. This applies to every covering map and locally closed stratum, with no finiteness or smoothness condition on $h$.

source.place: Ringed-topos pullback formula; coefficient-section compatibility from the cited node, using Bhatt-Scholze Lemma 5.4.1 only as geometric context

proof.text: For a finitely presented $A$-module $P$, choose a finite presentation $A^r\xrightarrow{B}A^s\to P\to0$ with scalar matrix $B$. By steps 2, 5 and 8 the local model $(p_U^*\underline A)\otimes_A P$ is sent to the cokernel of the identical matrix $A_U^r\xrightarrow{B}A_U^s$, namely the constant module sheaf $P_U$: the constant presheaf has this cokernel objectwise, and sheafification preserves its cokernel universal property by its left adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Conversely the inverse equivalence uses the identical presentation. Thus the same pro-etale cover trivializes the model in either description. Applying this on the same constructible locally closed strata proves equivalence of the constructibility predicates in [sk-def-sfb-constructible], on qcqs schemes and affine-locally on arbitrary schemes. Step 4 handles bounded cohomology and step 7 handles the Tor interval, so $D(E_T)$ identifies their bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategories. Finite $A$ makes every finitely presented $P$ finite; conversely a finite module over the finite ring $A$ has a finite presentation, since the kernel of a finite free surjection is a finite set and therefore finitely generated.

lean.statement:
theorem encoding_constructibility [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A]
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (e : Encoding A T) :
    (∀ M : Internal A T,
      HasFiniteConstantLocalModel (coefficient A) T M ↔
        ordinaryLocalModel A T ((e.ordinary.functor ⋙ e.fixed.functor).obj M)) ∧
    (∀ K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T),
      constantModelBoundedConstructible (coefficient A) T K ↔
        ordinaryBoundedConstructible A T (e.fixedDerived.functor.obj K))
